description: Rollout IW(1) is a depth-first form of IW(1) for problems where breadth-first layers are too wide, such as Atari games. It repeats random *rollouts*: walks down from the root, each step to a random child that is not *solved* (a solved node needs no more search). For each feature it keeps the smallest depth at which a node reached it. A rollout enters a new node only if the node reaches some feature at a smaller depth than before; otherwise it labels the node solved. Like IW(1), it reaches every goal of width 1, but its plans need not be shortest; this version runs until it finds a goal or the root is solved, while the paper uses it to choose actions within a time budget.

papers.authors: Wilmer Bandres, Blai Bonet, Hector Geffner
papers.title: Planning With Pixels in (Almost) Real Time
